questions.question: Which plant tissue carries water and dissolved minerals mainly from roots upward?
Which tissue transports sugars from sources to sinks in a plant?
What controls the opening of a leaf stoma?
What is pollination in flowering plants?
choices: Transfer of pollen to a stigma
Growth of a seedling from a seed

questions.question: Which flower structure contains ovules?
What usually develops from an ovule after fertilization?
What is a fruit in botanical terms?
choices: A mature ovary, sometimes with associated tissues

questions.question: Why do root hairs benefit a plant?
choices: They enlarge the stomata on each leaf
They increase surface area for water and mineral uptake
They transport most sugar from leaves to fruit

questions.question: How can closing stomata help during dry conditions?
choices: It increases carbon dioxide uptake while preventing any water loss
It increases water loss because leaves become warmer
It reduces water loss but can also limit carbon dioxide uptake
It increases root absorption enough to stop photosynthesis

questions.question: What is transpiration?
choices: Loss of water vapor from plant surfaces

questions.question: Why does a seed contain stored nutrients?
choices: They support early growth before the seedling can make enough food
They provide the embryo's only source of water
They replace the need for oxygen during germination
They keep the embryo dormant until all nutrients are gone

questions.question: How does vegetative reproduction differ from sexual reproduction?
choices: It always creates more genetic variation
It produces new plants without fusion of gametes
It requires pollen from two different species

questions.question: Why can seed dispersal away from a parent plant be useful?
choices: It makes every offspring genetically different from its parent
It guarantees arrival in a suitable habitat
It can reduce competition for light, water, and nutrients
It prevents offspring from needing sunlight

questions.question: What distinguishes fertilization from pollination?
choices: Fertilization releases seeds; pollination grows roots
Fertilization makes leaves; pollination transports sugars
Fertilization absorbs water; pollination opens stomata
Fertilization joins gametes; pollination transfers pollen

questions.question: How does a root's response to gravity generally help a seedling?
choices: It guides roots toward soil resources
It directs roots toward pollen-producing flowers
It stops growth whenever soil is dark

questions.question: A flowering plant has many leaves but no pollen reaches its stigmas. Which process is directly limited?
A stem cutting forms a new plant without fertilization. How is it classified?
A ring of bark containing phloem is removed from a tree trunk. Which transport is most directly disrupted?
choices: Water movement through intact inner xylem
Sugar movement between leaves and roots

questions.question: Seeds germinate in moist conditions but not in otherwise identical dry conditions. What is the best supported conclusion?
choices: Water was necessary for germination under these conditions
Water alone is sufficient for every seed to germinate
Moisture prevents the embryo from using stored food
Dry conditions supply all requirements for germination

questions.question: Two same-species plants reproduce sexually. Compared with making cuttings of one plant, what is generally expected?
choices: Offspring identical to the cutting parent in every case
More combinations of inherited alleles in offspring
Fewer allele combinations because gametes never differ
Offspring with alleles from only one parent in every case
